1inj5lf: This week you're in San Salvador. Your friends write to you: «¿Querés subir al volcán el sábado?». To reply you need very common verbs that change a vowel: **querer**, **poder**, **preferir**, **jugar**…
13q2kfp: Verbs that change the vowel: e → ie, o → ue, u → ue, e → i
1ehuju8: Some verbs change the last vowel of the stem when that syllable is **stressed**. _Querer_ → **quie**ro; _poder_ → **pue**do; _jugar_ → **jue**go; _pedir_ → **pi**do. The endings are the usual ones (-o, -es, -e, -emos…).
rupr70: Why only in some persons? Because in **nosotros** and **vosotros** the stress moves to the ending: que-**re**-mos, po-**de**-mos. The stem is no longer stressed and doesn't change. That's why people talk about the "shoe" or "boot" pattern: if you draw the table and mark the forms that change, it looks like a boot.
1ua66e5: There are four groups. **e → ie**: querer, preferir, empezar, entender, pensar, cerrar. **o → ue**: poder, volver, dormir, almorzar, costar, encontrar. **u → ue**: only _jugar_. **e → i** (only -ir verbs): pedir, repetir, servir.
14p8a3g: The dictionary doesn't warn you. That's why it's a good idea to learn these verbs with a label: _querer (ie)_, _poder (ue)_, _pedir (i)_.
1o5pdg1: Quick trick: if the **nosotros** form is regular and the **yo** form changes, you have a "boot" verb. Always practice out loud: qu**ie**ro, qu**ie**res, qu**ie**re, queremos.
1ax6tci: The "boot" pattern: the forms that change are in bold
9j0trr: _Poder_ changes **o → ue** in the stressed syllable: p**ue**do.
cgxjxm: With _nosotros_ the stem isn't stressed, so it doesn't change: **queremos**.
lcz4xk: With **querer** you say what you want, with **poder** what is possible for you, and with **preferir** what you choose between two options. All three can go with an **infinitive**: the second verb is not conjugated.
169ef9d: The structure is simple: conjugated verb + infinitive. **Quiero ver** a movie. **¿Puedes jugar** on Saturday? **Prefiero nadar** in the pool. There is no word between the two verbs: not _a_, not _de_, not _que_.
cvh5q9: If the infinitive is reflexive (levantarse, acostarse, ducharse), the pronoun goes **attached to the end** of the infinitive or **before the first verb**: _Quiero levantar**me** tarde_ = _**Me** quiero levantar tarde_. Both forms are correct.
o2r7tx: To say you can't, add a reason: _No puedo, **es que** trabajo el sábado_. **Es que** introduces an explanation and sounds kinder.
1oomcln: After _querer_ the second verb is in the **infinitive**: _ir_.
1kw8xhi: Between _poder_ and the infinitive there is no preposition.
1f8pyh1: _Levantarse_ is reflexive: the pronoun **me** doesn't disappear.
y58e3c: Vos querés, vos podés: voseo in Central America
17hvq6o: In El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, and Costa Rica, many people use **vos** with friends and family, just like in Argentina and Uruguay. In this course you learn **tú** as the main form, but you will hear _vos_ on the street and in messages.
mustmm: The good news: with **vos** these verbs **don't change the vowel**. The form looks like the infinitive and has an accent mark at the end: querer → **vos querés**, poder → **vos podés**, jugar → **vos jugás**, preferir → **vos preferís**, pedir → **vos pedís**.
1yyv707: The same happens with regular verbs: **vos trabajás**, **vos comés**, **vos vivís**. With reflexive verbs, the pronoun is **te**: _¿A qué hora te levantás?_
d9hta7: Tú and vos mean the same thing. In San Salvador you also hear **usted** among friends and in the family: it's a way of showing affection and respect, not distance.
nfmuvk: If you hear a form with an accent mark at the end and no vowel change (_podés, jugás_), it's almost certainly **vos**.
1vkmw03: Tú and vos in the present
rj0ksy: With _vos_ the stress falls on the ending, so the stem doesn't change: **querés**.
ox0ngl: To **suggest** something to a person, use a question with _querer_ or _poder_: **¿Quieres jugar al fútbol?** **¿Puedes el sábado?** To suggest something we do together, use **¿Por qué no…?** + a verb in _nosotros_: **¿Por qué no comemos pupusas?**
1op87pm: To **accept**: **¡Sí, claro!**, **¡Buena idea!**, **¡Perfecto!** Each region has its own quick word: **¡Va, pues!** in El Salvador and Honduras, **¡Dale!** in Central America and the Río de la Plata, **¡Vale!** in Spain, **¡Sale!** or **¡Va!** in Mexico.
19732sq: To **say no** politely, there are three steps: express regret (**Lo siento**), explain (**es que…**), and suggest something else (**¿Y el domingo?**, **Prefiero…**). A bare _no_ without an explanation sounds abrupt in Spanish.
jirhck: To wrap up the plan, confirm the day, the time, and the place: _Entonces, el sábado a las ocho. ¿Dónde **está** el parque?_

1alkxyu: The **ñ** is a letter of its own in Spanish. To pronounce it, press the middle of your tongue against the hard palate and let the air out through your nose. It is similar to the _ny_ in _canyon_, but it is **a single sound**: _ma-ña-na_, not _man-ya-na_.
1621tih: **N** and **ñ** tell words apart: _cana_ (white hair) and _caña_ (cane), _pena_ and _peña_, _mono_ and _moño_. If you don't separate them, you change the meaning.
10kv0kl: **LL** and **Y**: in most of the Spanish-speaking world they sound the same (this phenomenon is called **yeísmo**). _Calle_ and _cayó_, _pollo_ and _poyo_ have the same sound, similar to the _y_ in _yes_ but a little stronger.
6w0o9s: Real variation: in Buenos Aires and Montevideo, **ll** and **y** sound like the _sh_ in _show_ or the _s_ in _vision_: _yo me shamo_. In the relaxed speech of El Salvador and Honduras, the **ll** between vowels can sound very soft or almost disappear: _ga(y)ina_, _sía_ for _silla_. All of these pronunciations are correct in their region.
o3azg4: The **ñ** is always written with a tilde: if you don't have a Spanish keyboard, don't replace it with _n_ or _ny_. **Ll** and **y** sound the same for many people, so you have to learn the spelling word by word: _calle_, _playa_. At the end of a word, the _i_ sound is written **y**: _hoy, muy, soy_.
kqr7lr: A single sound: ma-**ña**-na. Don't say _man-ya-na_ with two sounds.
g5yrgt: Four ñ's in one sentence. Go slowly and keep your tongue against the palate.
